key_insight: This paper argues that MoE routing is not just an implementation detail—it can be actively explored during reinforcement learning to increase rollout diversity and improve learning. By perturbing expert selection, the model can generate more varied sparse computation paths and potentially better post-training outcomes.
problem_solved: Existing RL methods for Mixture-of-Experts models mainly optimize stability and efficiency while keeping expert routing fixed. This work addresses the missed opportunity of using expert selection itself as a controllable source of diversity during RL training.
method: Analyze how expert routing affects output diversity in MoE reinforcement learning.
Introduce expert-space exploration by perturbing routing decisions to sample different sparse expert paths.
Use the resulting routing diversity to enrich rollouts and improve RL training signal quality.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new lever for improving MoE post-training beyond optimizer tweaks and stability tricks. It could help produce stronger, more diverse policies with little added architectural complexity.

paper_title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Hongyi He, Zhenghao Lin, Xiao Liu, Peng Cheng, Yan Lu
